newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST-Siam Cement Q1 net seen higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Siam Cement Q1 net seen higher.

text.p: Thailand's largest industrial conglomerate, Siam Cement Plc, is expected to maintain its higher consolidated profit in the first quarter due to increased cement production capacity and improving earnings from its paper and steel units, analysts said on Friday.

But the earnings growth would be slower than it was in the same quarter a year ago as the sluggish economy has begun to take its toll on the group's revenue from building materials and cement, analysts said.

"Siam Cement will continue to post a rise in first quarter net profit, but at a slower rate of five to six percent (over the same quarter last year)," Visit Ongpipattanakul, investment analyst at HSBC James Capel Asia, told Reuters.
Siam Cement is a diversified industrial group with various businesses such as cement, pertrochemical, paper, electronics and car parts.

Thailand's economy is officially forecast to grow 6.8 percent this year, but analysts said recent turmoil in the financial sector, high interest rates and slow export growth could cap growth to well below that projection.
"The sluggish economy will certainly affect the group's sales from building materials," Visit said.
In the first quarter last year, the industrial group posted a 20 percent rise in net profit to 2.64 billion baht ($101.5 million) from 2.19 billion in the same period the year before.
Visit at James Capel projected Siam Cement to have a consolidated profit of 7.3 billion baht this year compared with 6.8 billion in 1996.
The higher earnings this year will be mainly supported by the rise in its cement production capacity by 4.2 million tonnes to a total of 21 million tonnes, analysts said.
The additional cement production came on stream late in the fourth quarter last year, they added.
"The company is our only buy (recommendation) in the cement (stocks). On an earning basis, it (share prices) looks cheap already," said an analyst at Capital Nomura Securities.
Siam Cement closed down 20 baht at 612 on Friday.
Capital Noumura expected Siam Cement to have a consolidated profit of 7.55 billion baht in 1997.
Analysts said the higher pulp and paper prices as well as improving performance from its steel units will also maintain the group's earning rise in the quarter.

"The group's profit from the pulp and paper division is expected to double compared with in the first quarter last year. Pulp and paper prices are improving," said one analyst at a U.S. investment house.
Siam Cement's steel subsidiaries, which posted a big loss last year, are expected to have higher sales after the government's enforcement of anti-dumping measures, analysts said.

Thai government last December imposed an additional 25.90-51.99 percent tariff on top of an earlier 10-20 percent level on structural steel from some countries following complaints by local producers of cheaper imports from those countries.
